Use Tier 2: add an order-aware residual sequence encoder to the current attentive similarity model. The latest model scored 0.4412 macro HR@10 versus the SASRec baseline’s 0.505, suggesting that discarding purchase order may have removed useful predictive information. This experiment will test that hypothesis while retaining the existing candidate-conditioned attention mechanism.

The affected components are model_design and training_evaluation. Add learned positional embeddings and one causal Transformer block over the history embeddings, masking padding and preventing attention to future interactions. Combine the encoded representation with each original context embedding through a learned residual gate before the existing candidate-conditioned attention and similarity calculation. This preserves direct item similarity while allowing the model to distinguish recent purchase intent from older preferences. Keep the existing training examples, sampled-softmax loss, negative sampling, optimizer, and hyperparameters fixed to isolate the architectural change.

Train separate models for all four categories using seed 42 and the unchanged input splits. Select checkpoints using validation HR@10 with 200 users, 99 unique unseen negatives, and evaluation seed 42, then report the four-category macro average. Update the checkpoint configuration and predictor writer to reconstruct the added encoder and use identical history processing during validation and host inference. Keep DATA_DIR as os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], save artifacts beneath the trial directory, and leave hidden test prediction generation to the host evaluator.
